I’d make this a **ranked list with animated horizontal bars**. Each row shows a position, identity and amount, with a bar behind it to make differences easy to compare. That gives us room for playful motion while keeping names and figures readable.

The page could have these components:

| Component | Proposed behavior |
|---|---|
| Landing-page link | A prominent “Explore the rankings” link near the main search. |
| Board selector | Four choices: MPs, Individuals, Companies and Parties. Always visible above the board. |
| Period selector | “Current term” and “All records”, with the selected period clearly stated. |
| Leaderboard | Top 10 initially. Rank, portrait or entity icon, linked name, secondary detail and exact amount. |
| Context beneath the board | What the amounts include, data freshness and any incomplete totals. |

For MPs, secondary detail could show party and constituency. For funders, it could show recipient or declaration counts where available. On mobile, the amount sits beneath the name so long names have room.

I’d keep the existing purple for MPs and teal for funders. Parties could use a small party-color marker alongside their name. The existing buttons, badges, identity indicators and loading states give us a starting point. The animated leaderboard would be a new reusable component.

There are two quite different animation directions:

- **An animated snapshot.** On entry, rows appear with a short stagger and bars grow into place over roughly half a second. Changing the period smoothly moves retained entries to their new positions. Changing entity type fades the old board out and introduces the new one. The board then stays still for reading.
- **A race through time.** A play/pause button and date slider advance through historical snapshots. Bars grow and rows overtake one another as declarations accumulate. This needs a visible date, replay controls and a clear definition of which date drives the race.

My recommendation is the snapshot for the first version. Applying the skill’s *Experience First* principle, I’d concentrate the polish on switching boards and watching positions settle. A historical race deserves its own deliberate playback experience. Both should respect reduced-motion preferences and keep final amounts readable throughout.

One wording detail matters before implementation. The project’s financial contract uses **“declared amounts”**, because records can include rates and benefits. I’d label the MP board “Highest declared amounts”. We should also establish whether “donations” means donations specifically or broader declared funding, and keep companies distinct from other organisations.

**When you picture the animation, do you mean rows racing through time with play/pause controls, or a current leaderboard that animates when opened and when you change the selection?**
